name: Ocrelizumab
route_note: IV infusion every 6 months; twice-yearly subcutaneous injection with hyaluronidase

discovery.note: Humanised IgG1 anti-CD20 antibody derived from murine antibody 2H7, binding an epitope overlapping that of rituximab.

tagline: Twice-yearly anti-CD20 antibody and first drug approved for primary progressive MS
summary: Ocrelizumab is a humanised anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody that depletes B cells. Given every six months, it is a highly effective therapy for relapsing multiple sclerosis and was the first drug approved for primary progressive MS.
mechanism: Ocrelizumab binds CD20 on B cells and depletes them mainly through antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and phagocytosis, with less complement-dependent cytotoxicity than rituximab.

B cells contribute to MS through antigen presentation, pro-inflammatory cytokines and formation of meningeal follicle-like structures. Their depletion reduces new inflammatory lesions and relapses; plasma cells, which lack CD20, are spared.
uses: Relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (including clinically isolated syndrome)

history.title: Rheumatoid arthritis and lupus programmes stopped
history.detail: Development in RA and lupus is halted because of serious infections.

history.title: OPERA and ORATORIO
history.detail: Phase 3 results show superiority over interferon beta-1a in relapsing MS and slower disability progression in PPMS.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved in March for relapsing MS and PPMS, the first PPMS therapy.

history.title: EU approval
history.detail: Approved in the European Union in January.

history.title: Subcutaneous form
history.detail: FDA approves Ocrevus Zunovo, a 10-minute twice-yearly subcutaneous injection.

pk.metabolism: Proteolytic catabolism to peptides and amino acids (no CYP metabolism)
pk.excretion: Not renally excreted as intact antibody; cleared by catabolism and target-mediated uptake

facts: Ocrelizumab was the first drug approved by the FDA for primary progressive multiple sclerosis.
Vaccines are best given before starting because B-cell depletion blunts vaccine responses.
